desc: Implement mapping from (x,y) to perimeter coordinate t (bottom: t=x; right: t=side+y; top: t=2*side+(side-x); left: t=3*side+(side-y)) and verify the Manhattan-vs-arc subtlety: reduction is valid only because k>=4 forces answer <= L/k <= side, and for d <= side the conflict relations coincide (same/adjacent edges: Manhattan = arc; opposite edges: both >= side >= d).
Sort points by t and build doubled array t2 = t + [ti + L] for wraparound handling.
Write feasible(d): build successor array nxt via two pointers in O(n), then greedy from every start s with k-1 jumps, failing on index >= s+n or wrap gap t2[s]+L-t2[pos] < d.
Binary search d over [1, L//k] (lo=1 always feasible; hi=L//k is the pigeonhole upper bound and <= side since k>=4).
Validate against the three examples (expect 2, 1, 1) and edge cases: all points on one edge, k = n, side = 1, clustered points (answer 1), and a case with d near side involving opposite-edge pairs.
Finalize code within the starter class with imports (bisect, List) and confirm complexity O((n + n*k) log(side)) ~ 12.5M ops.
